claim.pdf_says: 14.9.18.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading under 14.9.18 GOBACK statement, identical in rank to 14.9.18.1/.2/.3.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.18.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27389 — level 2, while its siblings '### 14.9.18.1 General', '### 14.9.18.2 General format' and '### 14.9.18.3 Syntax rules' are level 3)
claim.why_it_matters: Within a single clause the four sub-clauses are transcribed at two different heading levels, so General rules renders as a sibling of the GOBACK statement clause rather than as its fourth sub-clause. The outline nesting and clause-to-section mapping are wrong.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both sources. PDF page 662 (printed page 632), rendered at 300 dpi, shows the bold heading '14.9.18.4 General rules' immediately after syntax rule 8) 'Literal-1 shall not be a zero-length literal.' I also rendered the preceding page 661 (printed 631) to check rank rather than assume it: it carries '14.9.18 GOBACK statement', '14.9.18.1 General', '14.9.18.2 General format' and '14.9.18.3 Syntax rules' in the same bold run-in style, so 14.9.18.4 is unambiguously the fourth sub-clause of 14.9.18, identical in rank to .1/.2/.3 (the four-part numbering alone settles this). In specs/ISO_COBOL.md the heading is transcribed as '## 14.9.18.4 General rules' (level 2) while lines 27325 / 27330 / 27355 carry '### 14.9.18.1 General', '### 14.9.18.2 General format', '### 14.9.18.3 Syntax rules' (level 3) and line 27322 carries '## 14.9.18 GOBACK statement' (level 2). So in the markdown outline General rules is a peer of the GOBACK statement clause instead of its child — a real structural defect, not reflow, hyphenation or a page-break artifact. I checked each rejection ground and none applies: no text is absent or reflowed onto an adjacent line, the heading text matches the PDF verbatim, and the defect is not page-break furniture. Caveats that qualify but do not overturn the finding: (a) nothing is actually 'missing' — the heading is present and correctly worded, so kind=missing-heading is a misnomer for what is really a wrong-heading-level; (b) the claim's line number is off — the heading is at line 27392, with its anchor at 27391, not 27389; (c) the anchor '' is present and correctly formed, matching the sibling anchors, so anchor-based cross-referencing and any id-driven clause-to-section mapping still resolve — only nesting derived from heading DEPTH is wrong; (d) the defect is systemic rather than page-local: 162 four-part clause headings across the file are at level 2 versus 620 at level 3, so this is one instance of a file-wide heading-level artifact. Within clause 14.9.18 the .4 is the sole offender, and the immediately neighbouring 14.9.16.4 and 14.9.17.4 are correctly at level 3, which is what makes the inconsistency visible here. No normative content is altered.
verdict.corrected_description: Wrong heading level, not a missing heading. The PDF (page 662, printed 632) prints '14.9.18.4 General rules' as the fourth sub-clause of 14.9.18 GOBACK statement, in the same bold style as 14.9.18.1/.2/.3 on the preceding page. The markdown transcribes the heading text correctly and verbatim, with a correct '' anchor, but emits it at heading level 2 ('## 14.9.18.4 General rules', specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27392 — the claim cites 27389) while its three siblings are at level 3, making it a peer of '## 14.9.18 GOBACK statement' in any depth-derived outline. Anchor-based cross-references are unaffected; only heading-depth nesting is wrong. This is one instance of a file-wide artifact: 162 four-part clause headings are at level 2 against 620 at level 3, so the fix should be a systematic re-levelling sweep rather than a one-line patch on page 662.
